title: Github Actions
summary: GitHub Actions runs checks for you every time code changes: workflows written in YAML, triggered by events (push, pull request, manual), made of jobs and steps, with logs in the Actions tab. It's the CI part of DevOps. The step-by-step arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Write a GitHub Actions workflow that runs on push and runs a test suite, and debug it from the Actions tab.

steps.title: Read both lessons
steps.detail: Skim Intro to Workflows and Managing Workflows. Learn the four layers: event → workflow → job → step. Also learn runs-on: ubuntu-latest and workflow_dispatch (a manual run button).
steps.doneWhen: You can label each part of a small workflow YAML file.

steps.title: Read a workflow file
steps.detail: Workflows live in .github/workflows/*.yml. This minimal one matches the curriculum's Hello Workflows idea: run on every push to any branch, on Ubuntu, and echo a message. Don't commit it anywhere yet. Just read it and look up any line you don't know.
steps.code:
name: Hello Workflows
on:
  push:
    branches: ['**']
jobs:
  hello:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "Hello Workflows"
steps.doneWhen: You can say what triggers it, where it runs, and what it prints.

steps.title: Note the listed assignments
steps.detail: The curriculum lists Part I: Hello Workflows, a new repo whose workflow runs on every push to any branch, on Ubuntu, and echoes Hello Workflows. Part II: go back to earlier assignments with test suites and add workflows that run them. Myflix's npm test (Vitest) is a natural Part II candidate. Wait for Slack to confirm.
steps.doneWhen: You have a list of your repos that have test suites.

concepts.meaning: A YAML file in .github/workflows/ that says when to run what.
What starts a workflow: push, pull_request, schedule, or workflow_dispatch (manual).
A job runs on one machine (runner); steps are its commands, in order.
The fresh virtual machine GitHub gives a job, e.g. ubuntu-latest.
Where each run's pass/fail and logs show up on GitHub.

sources: Step 2's YAML is an illustration written for this guide, not from the curriculum
